all_limitations: This is a reconstruction of attributed statements and reasoning from the supplied target judgment, not independently verified pleadings, deeds, witnesses, trial exhibits, or judicial approval of a universal rule.

The defendants' joint-family title/co-ownership assertion and defendant no. 4's fraud/no-consideration plea are preserved as unresolved party positions, not negative proof of the landlady's possessory standing.

The historical High Court and Nagpur interpretations concern Section 9 of the 1877 Act; the Supreme Court expressly linked its first paragraph to Section 6(1) of the 1963 Act and rejected contrary restrictive holdings.

Section 6(1) conditions concerning dispossession without consent and otherwise than in due course of law, and Section 6(2) six-month filing limit and government exclusion, remain outside the standing and joinder conclusions; no independent filing date or complete proof of those elements is supplied.
